sourceBaseline.edition: 2024 U.S. Code for statutory text; later legal changes require validation
sourceBaseline.note: A learning reference pack, not a certified current-law database or a complete bill.

scope: Dated, source-linked American copyright and computational learning precedents; no non-U.S. laws.

authorities.title: Copyright Clause
authorities.relevance: Congress may grant exclusive rights for limited times to promote the progress of science and useful arts.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The clause empowers Congress; it does not itself resolve specific fair-use defenses or grant a universal right to machine learning.

authorities.title: Definitions and fixation
authorities.relevance: Fixation requires embodiment sufficiently stable for longer than a transitory duration.
authorities.scopeLimitations: This definition alone does not establish that every computer buffer is excluded from reproduction rights; context and duration matter.

authorities.title: Subject matter and exclusions
authorities.relevance: Facts, ideas, procedures, processes, systems and methods are excluded from copyright protection.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The underlying expression used to convey excluded subject matter can nonetheless remain protected.

authorities.title: Exclusive rights
authorities.relevance: Copyright owners have enumerated rights over reproduction, distribution, derivative works and specified performances and displays.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The rights are subject to Title 17 limitations and exceptions; they do not create a general property right in acquired knowledge.

authorities.title: Fair use
authorities.relevance: Fair use considers purpose, nature, amount, and market effect, including teaching, research and scholarship.
authorities.scopeLimitations: Commerciality and educational purpose are considerations, not automatic conclusions; all applicable factors matter.

authorities.title: Libraries and archives
authorities.relevance: Specified libraries and archives may make certain reproductions under statutory conditions.
authorities.scopeLimitations: This section is institution- and purpose-specific; it does not establish a universal right to digitize collections.

authorities.title: First sale
authorities.relevance: Ownership of a lawfully made tangible copy can permit its disposition without a new distribution license.
authorities.scopeLimitations: First sale does not independently authorize creating additional digital reproductions when transferring a copy.

authorities.title: Teaching and specified performances
authorities.relevance: Enumerated exceptions include face-to-face nonprofit classroom teaching, qualified mediated instruction and limited household film filtering.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The principal §110(1) classroom exemption expressly specifies nonprofit educational institutions; for-profit teaching is not categorically exempt.

authorities.title: Ephemeral recordings
authorities.relevance: Specified transmitting organizations can make ephemeral recordings under detailed conditions.
authorities.scopeLimitations: These exceptions are purpose- and entity-specific; their time limits do not create a general computer-copy exemption.

authorities.title: Computer programs
authorities.relevance: Owners of qualifying program copies may make certain copies essential to use and maintain software.
authorities.scopeLimitations: Eligibility and ownership conditions matter, and this is not blanket permission to reproduce arbitrary media.

authorities.title: Accessible format copies
authorities.relevance: Eligible entities may make and distribute accessible-format works for qualifying persons under conditions.
authorities.scopeLimitations: Accessible-format permissions have specific beneficiaries, entities and restrictions; not all disability-related copying is covered.

authorities.title: Transient digital transmissions
authorities.relevance: Qualified online service providers can obtain a conditional liability safe harbor for transient network communications.
authorities.scopeLimitations: A liability safe harbor does not independently authorize unlawful content acquisition, training or redistribution.

authorities.title: System caching
authorities.relevance: Qualified system caching can obtain a conditional liability safe harbor.
authorities.scopeLimitations: Conditions apply; §512 is not a general copying license or all-purpose defense to infringement.

authorities.title: Interoperability and access control
authorities.relevance: Limited anticircumvention provisions permit specified interoperability research on computer programs.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The exception is narrow and does not authorize general circumvention, intrusion, or access to any protected source.

authorities.title: Baker v. Selden
authorities.relevance: Distinguishes a copyrighted explanation of a system from the system itself.
authorities.scopeLimitations: Does not authorize duplication of expressive portions of the copyrighted book.

authorities.title: Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone
authorities.relevance: Facts lack copyright originality; originality in selection or arrangement can be protected.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The case does not hold that any work combining facts and original expression may be freely copied.

authorities.title: Sony Corp. of America v. Universal City Studios
authorities.relevance: Private household time-shifting was held fair use in its record; technological tools can have substantial noninfringing uses.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The decision addressed a particular consumer recording practice and does not authorize all machine-learning datasets.

authorities.title: Sega Enterprises v. Accolade
authorities.forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Ninth Circuit
authorities.relevance: Necessary intermediate copying to examine software functionality could be fair use despite the commercial context.
authorities.scopeLimitations: Reverse engineering for interoperability is materially narrower than all-purpose model training or output substitution.

authorities.title: Sony Computer Entertainment v. Connectix
authorities.forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Ninth Circuit
authorities.relevance: Intermediate copies of PlayStation BIOS during emulator reverse engineering were fair use on the specific facts.
authorities.scopeLimitations: An emulator without protected BIOS content in the product differs from a system retaining and distributing expressive source material.

authorities.title: Cartoon Network LP v. CSC Holdings
authorities.forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
authorities.relevance: The brief automatically overwritten buffers at issue did not yield fixed copies under the applicable statutory definition.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The opinion did not establish a universally lawful 1.2-second limit, or exempt independent later reproductions.

authorities.title: Authors Guild v. HathiTrust
authorities.forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
authorities.relevance: Full-text indexing and identified accessibility uses of digitized books qualified as fair use.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The holding concerns those functions and restrictions; it does not authorize broad distribution of the original books.

authorities.title: Authors Guild v. Google
authorities.forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
authorities.relevance: Copying whole books for indexed full-text search and limited snippets was fair use despite commercial operation.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The system did not give users substantial substitutes for the protected books; outputs that substitute may present different issues.

authorities.title: Fox News Network v. TVEyes
authorities.forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
authorities.relevance: A media monitoring service's availability of extensive broadcast clips for customer viewing failed fair-use analysis.
authorities.scopeLimitations: A useful search function did not immunize separately consumable news footage; the decision does not eliminate all search-engine fair use.

authorities.title: Google LLC v. Oracle America
authorities.relevance: Copying specific Java API declaring code in the Android development circumstances was fair use.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The Court assumed copyrightability for purposes of decision and did not authorize unrestricted software or media copying.

authorities.title: Andy Warhol Foundation v. Goldsmith
authorities.relevance: The first fair-use factor may weigh against a commercial licensing use serving substantially the same purpose as the original image.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The holding evaluated the specific magazine licensing use; it did not decide all transformative or learning scenarios.

authorities.title: Bartz v. Anthropic PBC
authorities.forum: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
authorities.relevance: The court held particular LLM book-training uses fair while distinguishing the pirated permanent library's retention.
authorities.scopeLimitations: This is a district-court ruling on a specific evidentiary record, not a categorical license for all AI training or unlawful acquisition.

authorities.title: Kadrey v. Meta Platforms
authorities.forum: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
authorities.relevance: Meta prevailed on the particular fair-use claims, with the court emphasizing limits of plaintiffs' market-harm evidence.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The court expressly did not hold that all LLM training is fair use; sufficiently supported displacement evidence could matter.

authorities.title: Thomson Reuters v. ROSS Intelligence
authorities.forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Third Circuit
authorities.relevance: The court rejected fair use of copied Westlaw editorial headnotes for a competing AI-assisted legal-research platform.
authorities.scopeLimitations: The opinion addressed a specific commercially overlapping search product and did not resolve all generative-model training controversies.
